description: Merhaba! Ekibimiz fizik mühendisliği ve işletme altyapısına sahip. Mars'ta astronotların hayatta kalması için güvenli rota ve güneş enerjisi şarj istasyonlarını birleştiren katmanlı bir harita konsepti geliştiriyoruz. Donanım simülasyonu, fizibilite ve görsel tasarım üzerine çalışıyoruz.
summary:
Astronauts exploring Mars face low solar irradiance, steep crater terrain, and sudden dust storms—making power loss or navigation errors life-threatening. To solve this, Team Khepri developed an integrated survival system combining an autonomous, dust-storm-protected solar charging station with a 3D Jezero Crater hazard and navigation map.

Placed along exploration routes, our Arduino-based solar tracker uses dual LDR sensors and a servo motor to follow sunlight, achieving up to 94% energy efficiency. When light drops below a storm threshold or an emergency occurs, the panel automatically folds flat (0° stow mode) to protect the hardware and triggers an audible alarm. Real-time sensor telemetry streams directly to a Python Mission Control dashboard layered over NASA MRO HiRISE imagery and MGS MOLA elevation data. This unified interface guides astronauts along safe corridors while avoiding steep cliffs, ensuring continuous power and route safety during Martian missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Project Khepri is an integrated survival and navigation system designed for astronauts exploring Jezero Crater on Mars. It combines an autonomous, route-based solar charging station with a real-time 3D Martian hazard and navigation dashboard.

The solar station uses an Arduino Uno R3, dual LDR light sensors, and an SG90 servo motor to continuously track sunlight along the astronaut's exploration route, achieving up to 94% energy efficiency. To survive sudden Martian dust storms, the system features an automated safety protocol: when ambient light drops below a storm threshold or an emergency push button is pressed, the solar panel automatically folds flat (0° stow position) to protect the hardware from dust accumulation and triggers an audible buzzer alarm alongside a status update on the I2C 16x2 LCD.

3D Jezero Crater Mapping & Telemetry:

Real-time sensor angles, efficiency metrics, and system alerts stream via serial telemetry to a Python Mission Control dashboard (built with Matplotlib and PySerial). This telemetry is layered over real NASA MRO HiRISE imagery and MGS MOLA digital elevation models of Jezero Crater, highlighting safe walking corridors, steep cliff hazards, and emergency escape routes.

Tools, Hardware & Software:

Hardware: Arduino Uno R3, SG90 Servo Motor, Dual LDR Sensors, I2C 16x2 LCD, Active Buzzer, Emergency Push Button.

Software & Simulation: Arduino IDE (C++), Python (Matplotlib, PySerial), Proteus 8 Professional (for pre-build circuit verification).

Datasets: NASA MRO HiRISE & MGS MOLA DEM (Jezero Crater).

Creativity & Design Factors:

Rather than relying solely on rover-mounted batteries, placing modular, storm-protected charging hubs along exploration routes minimizes the risk of power depletion. We prioritized low-power hardware reliability, automated mechanical stow protection, and clear visual hazard guidance for high-stress EVA (extravehicular activity) conditions.
